studies.title: Budgetary Equilibrium & Need vs Want Allocation
studies.summary: Need expenditure represents core baseline staples. Want expenditure represents discretionary lifestyle choices.
studies.advice: Keep Needs as the majority share (>50%) of total spend. When Wants exceed Needs, evaluate upcoming purchases with a 24-hour delay.

studies.title: Real-Time Micro-Transaction Friction
studies.citation: NotebookLM Section 3.1 — Real-Time Friction Behavioral Control
studies.summary: Impulse purchases occur when transaction friction is zero. Real-time categorization forces active decision making.
studies.advice: Always log purchases immediately at point-of-sale to preserve behavioral friction and habit reinforcement.

studies.title: Compensatory Budget Recovery
studies.summary: Overspending on a single day should be compensated by tightening discretionary Want spending on subsequent days.
studies.advice: If you exceed your daily budget today, reduce your daily Want target by 33% for the next 3 days until liquidity normalizes.

studies.title: Want Impulse Hold Protocol
studies.summary: Impulse Want purchases cluster when the Want share of the ledger is high and transaction friction is low.
studies.advice: When Wants reach or exceed half of weekly spend, hold new Want purchases for 24 hours before deciding.

studies.title: Daily Budget Health Check
studies.citation: NotebookLM Section 3.1 — Real-Time Friction Behavioral Control
studies.summary: A daily budget turns every purchase into an explicit trade-off against a visible limit.
studies.advice: When today's spend stays within the daily budget, keep logging at point of sale; the friction is the training.

studies.title: Need vs Want Ratio Benchmark
studies.summary: Ledgers with Needs above 50% of total spend show more stable cash-flow patterns.
studies.advice: Compare your weekly Need share against the 50% benchmark and shift future Wants when the ratio tilts.

studies.title: Weekend Spending Plan
studies.citation: NotebookLM Section 3.1 — Real-Time Friction Behavioral Control
studies.summary: Weekend spending spikes are predictable; a pre-committed Want cap reduces impulse leakage.
studies.advice: Plan the weekend ledger in advance: set a Want cap, keep Needs first, and log at point of sale.

studies.title: Consistency Streak Momentum
studies.citation: NotebookLM Section 3.1 — Real-Time Friction Behavioral Control
studies.summary: Consecutive logging days strengthen the categorization habit and damp impulse spending.
studies.advice: Protect the streak by logging every day; a streak of five or more days is the strongest habit signal.

studies.title: Goal-Based Period Comparison
studies.summary: Analyze-mode users benefit from comparing weekly Need and Want shares across periods.
studies.advice: When the spending goal is analyze, compare week-over-week shares and spot the trend before it becomes a pattern.
